chapter: A musical family and the old New Orleans bands
title: Chris Kelly, who never read music, and the Mobile trips
summary: Danny says plenty of New Orleans players couldn't read, and Chris Kelly was a great blues trumpeter whose plunger work impressed Mobile musicians.

story.theme_name: Remembering the early trumpeters and their styles
story.community_name: Chris Kelly, the blues trumpeter and his band

blocks.x: Now, they had just loads of musicians in New Orleans who couldn't play no music. They was all saying, "Nobody pay you to read no music; they pay you to play!"
That's what they said. As long as you could play like Chris Kelly -- and I don't think he ever had his hand on a piece of music.
One of the greatest Blues trumpet players ever happened. He used to go from New Orleans to Mobile. And when I seen Cootie playing that plunger, that's what

Chris Kelly used to do. Because when you'd go to Mobile, they'd talk of Gomez's Auditorium you played in. And when you played there, all the Mobile musicians went there and stood in front, just about ten deep looking at you, to see what you were doing. Because then they couldn't understand what this New Orleans thing was all about. Because it was hard for people to fake.
